stage1.impression: A symmetric, centred view over two tub-chair backs to a pair of speakers on oak plinths in a timber-framed niche, with an Orb lamp on a hexagonal table in the middle. It reads as a clean CG showroom or home-theatre render, not a photograph. The whole frame is under a milky veil with no true blacks. The chairs read as salmon plastic, the end-grain niche reads as a tiled grid, and the speakers are dim and grey, so they are not the hero. A magazine would see a generic hi-fi room, not a specific place.

blocking_9: True blacks: frame lum_p5 at 12 or below and lum_p1 at 6 or below (now 20.4), so the shadows are deep, not veiled
The speakers are the brightest objects apart from the lamp: speaker regions lum_median at 60 or more, with the light reading through the tinted acrylic and on the horn
Pools of light with dark between them: the niche felt and the end-grain wall fall to lum_median 22 or below away from the speakers
The Orb table top is not clipped (clip_pct below 1 %)
The foreground chairs read as espresso velvet (soft sheen, nap, dark), not pink plastic, and do not fill the bottom third
Off-axis, lived-in composition with props (a glass, a record out of its sleeve), so it reads as a specific bar and not a symmetric product shot
Material grain at 1:1: the end-grain blocks vary in tone and size and are not a regular grid; the oak shows grain and stain variation

defects.what: lifted blacks or veil across the whole frame: lum_p1 20.4, top band 0-40 has lum_range 7.3, so nothing goes dark; reads as haze plus a flat grade
Orb table top blown: clip_pct 15.5, lum_median 181; the lamp burns out its own table
left speaker dim and grey (lum_median 44, RGB 46/43/45), with no glow through the acrylic; the altar spot lands on the felt above it, not on the cabinet
right speaker the same (lum_median 42); the pair is not the hero
isolated hot specular blob on the left cabinet's edge reads as a CG highlight
left tub chair back: smooth, pink or salmon, featureless; reads as plastic, not espresso velvet; fills the lower left
right tub chair back the same; the two chairs block the lower third
end-grain block wall reads as a regular square tile grid (CG tiling), low contrast
felt panels behind the speakers are flat dark voids with no texture
spot beams show as hard CG cones in uniform haze
oak frame flat and uniform in tone, pinkish (R 66 G 45 B 40); little grain
perfect bilateral symmetry and no props in view: no sign of life, reads as a showroom

changes.problem: The frame has no blacks: a uniform veil lifts every shadow to about 22-27, which flattens the room and reads as CG.

evidence.measured: lum_p1 20.4, lum_p50 37.1; top band 0-40 lum_p5 27.1, range 7.3

change.to: AgX - High Contrast (or Punchy), haze 0.003/m, exposure 2.3 -> 2.1

changes.expected: Deep shadows in the corners and ceiling, the beams still faintly visible near the spots, and the frame median about 28-34

changes.problem: The altar spots light the felt and the niche above the speakers instead of the cabinets, so the speakers stay grey and dim.

evidence.measured: lum_median 44.1 (right 42.0), RGB about neutral 46/43/45; bright cones end above the cabinets at y about 100-180

change.from: 240 W, cone 30 deg, aimed into the niche
change.to: aim each at its speaker's cabinet centre (about 0.8 m up), cone 18 deg, 300 W, so the light passes through the smoked acrylic and grazes the horn

changes.expected: Each speaker is the brightest object after the Orb, glowing through its tint, with a soft pool on the plinth

changes.problem: The Orb is far too strong for its table and blows the top.
changes.expected: A warm, readable pool on the oak top, with grain visible and no clipping; the Orb's liner stays the brightest point

changes.problem: The dead-centre, symmetric view over two chair backs reads as a product shot, and the chairs hide the lower third and the plinths.

evidence.measured: the chair backs fill about 30 % of the frame; the composition is mirror-symmetric about x 360

change.to: [12.0, 2.3, 1.15] -> [16.4, 3.2, 1.0], 40 mm, f/2.8: off-axis and seated, one chair shoulder in soft foreground at the edge of the frame, the pair and the Orb table fully visible

changes.expected: A seated guest's view, with depth and asymmetry and the speakers larger in the frame

changes.problem: The espresso velvet tub chairs read as smooth salmon plastic under the Orb light.

evidence.measured: lum_p95 102.4, warm-pink highlights with no nap or sheen falloff (seen at 3x)

change.to: darker espresso base (about #2A1C16), sheen 0.6 with sheen tint 0.3, a fine nap normal map, roughness 0.8

changes.expected: Dark chairs with a soft rim sheen where the Orb catches them; they recede instead of dominating

changes.problem: The end-grain niche lining reads as a regular square tile grid with uniform tone.

evidence.measured: lum_range 34.4; a visibly repeating, equal-sized grid at 3x

change.setting: end-grain block finish (oak stain and variation)
change.to: per-block random tone ±15 %, growth rings per block, slightly irregular block sizes, darker smoked stain

changes.expected: It reads as real end-grain blocks under raking light, with the pools from the altar spots showing the texture

changes.problem: No sign of life in the zone; it reads as a showroom.

evidence.measured: only the Orb on the table; no glass, sleeve or coat anywhere in the frame

change.to: a half-drunk rocks glass and a record sleeve on the Orb table, a second sleeve leaning on a plinth, a coat over one chair arm

changes.expected: The Orb's light catches the glass and makes small highlights; the room reads as in use

changes.problem: The oak and the chairs carry a pink or magenta cast rather than warm amber.

evidence.measured: RGB median 66/45/40 on the oak; the chairs are similarly pinkish

change.to: tint +0.05 toward green; the oak stain shifted toward amber-brown and darkened about 20 %

changes.expected: Warm, brown neutrals in the room, so the speakers' tint is the only distinct colour

out_of_scope.request: Give the Smoke speakers a visibly saturated tint so they carry the frame's one colour
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's colour is fixed. Smoke is a near-neutral configuration, so this frame cannot meet the one-colour test except through light through the acrylic (c2).

out_of_scope.request: Simplify the visible internals behind the cabinet face, which read as cluttered
out_of_scope.why: The speaker's parts are fixed (cover off, batts inside).

out_of_scope.request: Break the symmetry of the altar itself (plinth heights, niche layout)
out_of_scope.why: The room's design is fixed; only the camera can break it (c4).
